newsitem.title: JAPAN: Summers did not request specific fiscal steps -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Summers did not request specific fiscal steps -- MOF.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters that U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers did not ask him in a meeting on Tuesday to take any specific fiscal steps.
Mitsuzuka spoke after a meeting with Summers in Tokyo.
Summers came to Tokyo to attend a "Six Markets" meeting between finance and central bank officials of Japan, the United States, Australia, Hong Kong, Singapore and China.
Asked whether Summers had asked Japan to take fiscal steps to stimulate the economy, Mitsuzuka said: "There were no such requests.
"We talked about various things and did not touch upon specifics of such policy," he told reporters.
In a speech last Friday, Summers warned Japan against trying to export its way out of its economic problems and urged it to restore domestic demand-led growth and repair its financial system.
U.S. officials are worried that Tokyo's plans to tighten budget policy, including raising its sales tax in April, could further undermine growth -- a concern Summers alluded to in his speech.
